name: _sparse_semi_structured_apply
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI, and not the whole contract): aten::_sparse_semi_structured_apply(Tensor input, Tensor thread_masks) -> (Tensor, Tensor). All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_sparse_semi_structured_apply(Tensor input, Tensor thread_masks) -> (Tensor, Tensor). This definition records only that one registered overload because the operator exposes exactly one schema (overloads() returns ['default']); other behaviour that is not expressible as a single signature remains owned by the original Gems pytest. The original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract - the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation it supports; do not narrow, delete or adapt those tests or reference behaviour to fit this one signature. Semantics derived from the tests: the operator applies a uint8 thread mask to a rank-2 activation tile. `input` is a rank-2 (M, K) tile with positive extents, M % 32 == 0 and K % 64 == 0, and dtype float16 or bfloat16 only; rank 0/1 fail with IndexError while rank >= 3 fails a dim() == 2 check with RuntimeError. Input-dtype rejection is asserted only on the backend where the rejection matrix was measured (flag_gems.vendor_name == 'nvidia'), where other input dtypes raise RuntimeError; on other backends those parameter sets are empty and pytest collects the tests as skipped, so no cross-backend dtype-rejection claim is made. `input` is read through its strides, so row-major tiles require stride(0) % 8 == 0 while column-major or 8-aligned second-stride tiles are accepted. `thread_masks` is a uint8 structural mask of shape (M / 8, K / 8, 8) with stride(1) == 8 and stride(2) == 1; a non-zero storage offset is accepted, it is read-only and its bytes must survive the call (the tests compare it against a pre-call clone), and no broadcast applies. Mask dtype rejection is likewise asserted only on that measured backend, where other mask dtypes raise RuntimeError; other mask extents raise RuntimeError. The two outputs are packed, independently oriented selections of the mask-selected input values: out0 has shape (M, K / 2) and out1 has shape (K, M / 2), both contiguous and in the input dtype, and out1 is not a transpose of out0. The representative signature uses positional-or-keyword tensor operands with no defaults and no omitted optional arguments; backward is not implemented for this operator.
